title: Car Fleet
statement: Cars drive on a one-lane road toward a target. Each car has a start position and a constant speed. A car cannot pass: if it catches a slower car ahead, it slows down and drives with it as a fleet. Count the fleets that reach the target.

example.caption: Target 12. The cars at 10 and 8 meet and travel together. The cars at 5 and 3 do too. The car at 0 is alone.

idea.sentence: Sort cars from the target backwards and compute each car's arrival time. A car that would arrive sooner than the fleet ahead joins it. Otherwise it starts a new fleet.

jargon.plain: Cars that end up driving together at the speed of the slowest one ahead. They reach the target at the same moment.
Hours to reach the target if the road were empty: (target - position) / speed.

watch.inputHint: Three arguments: target, positions, speeds, e.g. 12, [10,8,0,5,3], [2,4,1,1,3]

compare.bruteLabel: Simulate the road and merge cars again and again

rows.name: Simulate
rows.note: Move time forward, find collisions, merge cars. Hard to get right and slow.

rows.name: Sort + stack
rows.note: Sorting costs n log n. The pass after it is O(n). A car's fate depends only on the fleet directly ahead.

fast.takeaway: You never need to simulate the crash. Compare arrival times of neighbours, nearest car first.

stages.title: Arrival times, sorted
stages.note: Pair each position with its hours to the target, then sort the cars closest to the target first.

stages.title: Fleet stack
stages.note: Holds the arrival time of each fleet. The top is the fleet right ahead of the next car.

stages.title: Slower: new fleet
stages.note: If this car needs longer than the fleet ahead, it cannot catch up. Push its time.

stages.title: Faster: join
stages.note: If it needs less or equal time, it catches the fleet and slows down. Push nothing.

stages.title: Count fleets
stages.note: Each stack entry is one fleet. The answer is the stack size.

edges.title: One car
edges.why: Nothing is ahead, so it forms a fleet by itself.

edges.title: Arrive at the same time
edges.why: Both need 2 hours. Meeting exactly at the target counts as one fleet, so compare with strictly greater.

edges.title: Input not sorted
edges.why: Positions arrive in any order. Sort by position first, and keep each speed attached to its car.

edges.title: Huge numbers
edges.why: Times are 1 and 1 exactly. Both languages divide correctly rounded, so equal fractions give equal times.

gotchas.text: (target - pos) / speed with ints truncates. 7 / 2 is 3, so two different cars can look tied. Convert to float64 before dividing.
Array.sort with no comparator sorts as strings, so 10 comes before 2. Pass (a, b) => b.pos - a.pos.
Sort positions and speeds together. If you sort only positions, each speed ends up on the wrong car.
Use time > top, not >=. A car with exactly the same arrival time is part of that fleet.
A faster car behind a slower one does not pass it. It slows to the fleet speed, which is why only the arrival time of the fleet ahead matters.

recap.pattern: Sort, then stack of arrival times
recap.key: Go from the car nearest the target. A car arriving later than the fleet ahead starts a new fleet. Otherwise it joins.
recap.complexity: Time O(n log n). Space O(n).
moves: time = (target - position) / speed, as a float
Sort cars by position, closest first
Push time if it is strictly greater than the top
